Holzbaurechner / Fence

Wood fence calculator

Posts, rails, pickets and concrete for a wood privacy or picket fence, with a shopping list in stock lengths and a cost estimate.

How the fence is built

The calculator plans the classic American wood fence: 4x4 posts set in concrete, usually 8 ft apart, with 2x4 rails between them and dog-ear pickets nailed to the rails. Fences up to 4 ft get two rails per section, taller fences three. An 8 ft fence gets 6x6 posts.

Posts go about a third of the fence height into the ground, at least 2 ft. A 6 ft fence therefore uses 8 ft posts. Pickets end about 2 in. above the ground so they do not wick up water.

Privacy fence or picket fence

Set the gap to 0 for a privacy fence with pickets butted together. For a classic picket fence, 2 to 3 in. between 5-1/2 in. pickets is typical. Fresh pressure-treated pickets shrink as they dry, so a privacy fence built tight shows small gaps after the first summer.

Pressure-treated or cedar?

Posts should always be pressure-treated lumber rated for ground contact, even on a cedar fence. Cedar pickets and rails look better, are lighter and stay straighter, but cost about 40 to 50 % more. Pressure-treated pine is cheaper and takes stain once it has dried for a few months.

Building the fence step by step

  1. Rules first: check the property line, local height limits and HOA rules, and call 811 at least a few days before you dig.
  2. Lay out the line: drive stakes at the ends and corners and stretch a string line. Mark the post positions along it.
  3. Set the posts: dig the holes about three times as wide as the post, add a few inches of gravel, set the post plumb and fill with concrete. Fast-setting concrete is poured dry and then soaked with water.
  4. Rails: fasten the rails to the posts with brackets or structural screws, the top rail a few inches below the post top.
  5. Pickets: use a spacer block for even gaps and check with a level every few pickets. Two nails or screws per rail.

Frequently asked questions

How many pickets do I need for 100 ft of fence?
With 5-1/2 in. pickets butted together you need 219 pickets for 100 ft. With a 2 in. gap it drops to 160. Add a few percent for split or warped pickets.
How many bags of concrete per fence post?
For a 4x4 post in a 10 in. hole 2 ft deep you need two to three 50 lb bags of fast-setting concrete. The calculator works it out from the hole size.
How far apart should fence posts be?
8 ft is the standard, because rails come in 8 ft lengths. In windy areas or for tall privacy fences, 6 ft spacing makes the fence much sturdier.
Do I need a permit for a fence?
The model building code exempts fences up to 7 ft, but many cities set their own limits, often 6 ft in back yards and 3 to 4 ft in front yards, and some require a permit for any fence. Check with your city or county before you build.

Lumber sizes follow the span tables of the 2021 International Residential Code (IRC) and are planning values. They do not replace a permit review or an engineer. Decks, patio covers and carports usually need a building permit, so check with your local building department.
